key_insight: PointX predicts scene properties at 3D surface points rather than independently at image pixels. This makes the decomposition consistent when the same surface is seen from different viewpoints.
problem_solved: Recovering material properties, surface normals, and lighting from images is ambiguous. Pixel-based methods can assign conflicting properties to the same physical point across views.
method: Encode multiple unposed images using a multi-view transformer.
Use a feed-forward model to predict intrinsic properties per 3D surface point rather than per pixel.
Represent appearance through albedo, roughness, metallicity, surface normals, and irradiance.
impact: Point-based prediction offers a way to obtain coherent scene properties across views, potentially benefiting material estimation, relighting, and 3D content workflows. The supplied abstract is truncated and provides no quantitative results.
visual_elements: Several camera views linked to one shared point on a 3D surface.
Side-by-side illustration: conflicting per-pixel predictions versus a shared per-point prediction.
Pipeline diagram: unposed images → multi-view transformer → queried surface-point properties.
Property cards showing albedo, roughness, metallicity, normals, and irradiance.
paper_title: PointX: Multi-View Consistent Intrinsics by Querying Surface Points
paper_authors: Miguel Farinha, Sam Sartor, Iliyan Georgiev, Giuseppe Vecchio, Ronald Clark
